KnowledgeArticle.Title: Noise from Construction
KnowledgeArticle.Description: Report noise from street or building construction, including jackhammer noise.

Section.Name: Noise from Construction Intro
Section.Content:
Need something else?

  • Noise Complaints to report other types of noise
  • Noise Code to learn about the noise code and current noise reduction projects
  • Building Construction Complaint to report building construction activity that is unsafe, done after hours, outside approved plans, or done without a permit

You can report noise from construction, including jackhammering and construction activity during, before, or after hours.

Residential Construction is allowed between 7 AM and 6 PM on weekdays. Alterations or repairs to existing one-family or two-family, owner-occupied dwellings, convents or rectories may also be performed on Saturdays and Sundays between 10:00 AM and 4:00 PM.

Commercial, Street, and Highway Construction is allowed on weekdays between 7 AM and 6 PM. However, emergency work necessary for public safety, or work that cannot be performed during normal work hours may occur after hours or on weekends.

Work may take place at other times only if the site has a construction variance from the City.

You can report noise even if a site has a variance.

Report noise from:

Picture or Video Attachments

Picture or video attachments may be used for informational purposes only. A condition must be observed in person by a DEP inspector for a summons or Commissioner's order to be issued.

Section.Name: Construction Noise Reduction
Section.Content:
If you perform certain activities or use certain equipment at a construction site, you need to follow a noise mitigation plan to reduce the amount of noise from the site.

Learn about construction noise mitigation plans.

Section.Name: Noise Inspection Report
Section.Content:
If you have submitted a noise service request to the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP), and DEP has completed an inspection, you can request a Noise Inspection Report (NIR) be sent to you.

DEP responds to service requests for noise from:

  • Air Conditioner or Ventilation Equipment
  • Battery energy storage system (BESS)
  • Boats
  • Business Equipment
  • Chronic Alarms
  • Construction
  • Dog or Other Animals
  • Ice Cream Trucks
  • Lawn Equipment
  • Private Garbage Trucks
  • Wastewater Treatment Plants

To have the NIR sent to you, you must include:

  • The service request number
  • The date of DEP's inspection
  • An email or mailing address

The NIR will be sent to you 14 days after the inspection has been completed or 14 days after your request, whichever is later. Requests submitted with insufficient information cannot be fulfilled.

Online

Email DEP to request a Noise Inspection Report.

Use "Request for Information" as Message Type and "Noise Control" as Message Topic.

By Phone

Call 311 or 212-NEW-YORK (212-639-9675) for help.

Section.Name: DEP NYC Noise App
Section.Content:
NYC Noise is New York City’s Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) free iPhone and Android mobile app. The app will collect noise data for DEP to better understand noise levels, sources, and patterns.

The app does not submit noise complaint services requests.

NYC Noise is for data collection only. It provides DEP with:

  • Noise decibel level
  • Date, time, and source of noise
  • Defines noise by types:
    • Alarm
    • Car and bus traffic
    • Construction
    • Dog/animal
    • HVAC/fan
    • Loud music
    • Siren
    • Vehicle horn

Submitted data appears in map and table formats. Data will help DEP identify noise hotspots and guide their targeted enforcement efforts.

Learn more about DEP's NYC Noise App.
